newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Argo Investments 1st half net rises.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Argo Investments 1st half net rises.

text.p: Argo Investments Ltd said on Wednesday its attributable net operating profit rose 5.5 percent to a record A$17.23 million in the first half ended December 31 from A$16.32 million a year earlier.

"We are encouraged that most industrial companies have reported solid results in a weak economy and corporate balance sheets are very strong," managing director Rob Patterson said of the interim reporting season for Australian companies.
"Most economic forecasters are seeing an improving economy ahead which augurs well for second half profits," he said in a statement.
Argo declared a steady fully franked dividend of 6.5 cents a share.

Argo was capitalised at A$680 million and had some A$850 million in group funds under management at December 31, including those of smaller associated listed companies, Bounty Investments Ltd (Argo 30 percent) and Wakefield Investments (Australia) Ltd (35 percent), Argo said.

The company said it would again offer its share purchase plan to shareholders in May 1997, doubling the discount from market price to five percent, after last year raising A$19.8 million in new capital for investment.

Patterson said Argo liked to have a ready supply of cash to take advantage of gains which could be made from new floats, with several big offerings on the horizon including Optus Communications Pty Ltd, Australia's national telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp and the Australian Mutual Provident (AMP) Society.
